rules.reason: R-source-timing and R-history-view document source reuse, per-attempt subscriptions and synchronous navigation; F-view-owner separates captured audit attribution from current visit. Same data does not imply same visit. No added predicate or ungrounded ownership rule.

Task restoration and documented synchronous startup emission require reception eligibility before the initial emission. F-progress is the current defective ordering, not a requirement to preserve it. No concrete API or unique implementation is mandated.

R-history-view says no new admission after retirement, with no grace period. F-navigation and F-cancel show publication of a resource/remover after potentially reentrant startup. I-startup-window connects actual late-cancel and in-start stale audit traces to this temporal explanation. Logical invalidation independent of late physical cleanup is supported; no blanket cancellation policy or settlement deadline is introduced.

README 52-62/R-history-view explicitly retains exactly-once audit when already accepted decoding finishes after closing. F-view-owner separates audit from display. This rule does not gate already-admitted completion by current identity and does not permit new retired admission. The before-return persistence deadline from the prior rejected metadata is absent.

R-reentry and R-retry-entry preserve newer current-resource ownership, entry-bound accepted commands and cancellation/retry under synchronous callbacks. Source F-navigation/F-cancel/F-retry corroborate code placement. Rule preserves behavior, not a unique implementation.

R-source-timing/R-history-view permit the specific synchronous emission/reentry window. Full O-auto/O-dev schedules observe stale audit before old start returns. Actual selfchecks show old-source follow-up events only after outer select returns for the reentry test; that does not cover nested same-source reopen or in-start old emission. Verification asks for valid current progress and admitted late audit separately, with no reference patch or assertion-name-derived policy.

Task and R-format exclude queue record/public API extension; R-source-timing and R-reentry preserve source reuse, independent owners, accepted command history and native cancellation/retry/navigation semantics. Implementation can change to preserve behavior; no new adjacent policy.

applicability.reason: R-source-timing states the same source/file can serve multiple visits, distinct from each attempt subscription lifetime.
R-source-timing states each selected or retried attempt starts its own subscription to the shared source.
F-cancel constructs one native controller and cleanup handle per transfer attempt.
F-view-owner captures the admitted file/attempt tuple; R-history-view retains accepted event attribution after current visit changes. This does not demand copying arbitrary mutable objects.
R-history-view explicitly permits visible callback to synchronously select/hide.
R-history-view and F-view-owner separate retained audit from current-visit visible updates.
